messages:
Aisha: Opening thread - we need clarity on routing policy semantics for sticky sessions across hosted/dedicated/private. Current behavior: adapter sticks to hosted until a hard error, but there are subtle ordering/consistency problems when we failover mid-stream. Observed reordering for multi-part responses.
Liam: Saw that in prod yesterday. The client sent a 3-part stream, hosted started but then we routed remainder to dedicated; dedicated returned tokens without the same prefix KV, so the output was inconsistent.
Noah: Is the root cause session affinity loss or snapshot restore latency?
Aisha: Both. Affinity currently uses a best-effort ephemeral cookie in the control plane. If route decision flips we try to replay a snapshot, but there is no strong ordering guarantee that prevents duplicate or skipped chunks.
Priya: Proposed design options: 
1) Strong session affinity: guaranteed single runtime per logical session. Pros: consistent KV, simple semantics. Cons: capacity coupling and tail latency amplification; harder to failover gracefully.
2) Stateless request-by-request routing + idempotent reassemble layer: break responses into idempotent fragments with sequence ids and re-merge client-side. Pros: elastic routing; Cons: needs protocol changes and client/SDK updates.
3) Transactional snapshot handoff: take a short-lived transaction snapshot and apply atomically on target runtime before sending next chunk. Pros: preserves ordering and state. Cons: adds latency on failover and complex handshake.
Liam: We should quantify end-to-end cost. E.g., atomic snapshot handoff adds a 50-200ms tail on failover but keeps responses consistent. Strong affinity adds no extra per-request cost but leads to hot hosts.
Noah: Also consider partial consistency mode: allow best-effort restore but mark the response stream as degraded and attach a provenance header so client can decide. That helps PLG customers avoid silent quality regressions.
Priya: Agreed. Example routing DSL I sketched: 
```yaml
routing_policy:
  mode: hybrid # strong | stateless | hybrid
  affinity_ttl_ms: 300000
  fallback_behavior:
    restore_mode: transactional # best_effort | transactional | none
    degrade_header: X-Redwood-Fallback-Info
```
Aisha: For hybrid, semantics: prefer hosted with affinity; on failover attempt transactional restore if supported by target; otherwise best_effort and emit degrade header.
Liam: We need capability discovery on runtimes: they should advertise {supports_transactional_restore: bool, restore_latency_ms_p50: number, max_snapshot_size_bytes: number}. That lets control plane make cost-informed decisions.
Noah: Security note: transactional snapshots must be envelope encrypted and tenant-scoped; also snapshot application must validate session nonce to prevent replay.
Priya: Operational hooks: metrics for restore_success, restore_latency, fallback_stream_reorders, and a synthetic test that injects a mid-stream failover in staging to validate semantics.
Aisha: Edge-case: long-lived streams (minutes). Strong affinity may be necessary for low-latency interactive sessions (chat), whereas batch generation can be stateless with reassembly. Need per-route override in the DSL.
Liam: Implementation roadmap suggestion: 
- Phase 0: add capability discovery and emit metrics + degrade_header when fallback occurs (no snapshot).
- Phase 1: implement best_effort snapshot restore with opt-in per-customer.
- Phase 2: transactional snapshot protocol between adapter and runtime + server-side nonce validation.
- Phase 3: client/SDK reassembly support for stateless mode.
Priya: Backwards compat: older runtimes without transactional support are treated as supports_transactional_restore=false. Control plane should include a simulation mode to estimate cost impact before enabling strong affinity.
Noah: Tests: sequence integrity (no duplicate/skipped tokens), latency regression at various QPS, and security tests for replay and cross-tenant snapshot access.
Aisha: I'll draft an RFC addendum capturing DSL, capability schema, metrics, and phased rollout. Also opening INF-900 to track work.
InfraBot: Created ticket INF-900: "routing-policy-dsl-session-affinity-and-restore" -> https://redwood/INF-900
Liam: One more UX ask: Console should surface per-route default mode and let customers toggle route-level affinity and restore behavior. DevEx will need copy on tradeoffs.
Priya: I'll add the Console opt-in flag and the audit event shape to the RFC.
Aisha: Cool. Can we sync for 30 on Thursday to align on metrics and phase 0 owners?
Noah: I can take Phase 0 infra bits.
Liam: I'll own the DSL proto and RFC text.
Priya: Security review on Phase 1/2 from me.
Aisha: Thanks all. Meeting invite incoming. :thumbsup:
